questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to learn spanish and Chile was one of the safer options to choose from in South America. Also the nature.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: More or less. UCHILE had a lot prepared with online orientations before arrival and so on. On the other hand, a lot of that information was wrong and didn't apply to the facultuy of architecture.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The PME faculty had some orientations and introduction for PME- students at the "international faculty". I was not connected to the architecture faculty, and i therefore missed a lot of important information that would be relevant for me as a landscape architecture student only taking classes at that specific faculty.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Super easy. For the first 10 days we rented an airbnb, and after 5 days we already found housing. I would reccomend waiting until you arrive to book something, to get a feel of the different neighbourhoods first.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Websites like compartodepto are very easy. Here you're getting headhunted by landlords. I lived in a house with 9 other exchange students, which sometimes, was a bit much. But also a very good way to get to know people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of people stayed in the neighbourhood Providencia. Would't reccomend Vitacura or Las Condes even though those are the safests and richest areas, but it's soooo far away from where you're gonna have your daily life.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registration to UCHILE was simple, but registrations to courses was super complicated and confusing. Again because the faculties do things very differently. First of all, some of the course descriptions came out days before first day of class. You have to send an email to PME with the classes you want and then they will check with the FAU if its possible. Because pretty much every other architecture student is connected directly to FAU, they are first in the application process. For the first 1-2 weeks you just show up at the classes you're interested in and ask if it's possible to join, which sometimes it is and other times not.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The PME office was easy to go to, also teachers and other students

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I didn't get all the classes i wanted. Some of them were restricted if you were connected to PME and not FAU

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everyone is a bit confused. So just be a bit confused together and then you will figure it out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level was fine for me as my spanish was not my best. If you actually speak good spanish I would say the courses lean to the easier side, but it also really varies from course to course. Taller/design courses take a lot of your time.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It's very much listen to the teacher talk and take notes. You don't have one final exam at the end, but several tests during the semester. For these tests it's just about repeating what was said in class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Taller 7: Integración de variables de gestión, Geografía urbana, Electivo de especialización: Experimentos Urbanos: Estudios de Impacto del Entono Construido en el Comportamiento Humano, Español para Extranjeros

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would reccomend Taller 7 and Geografia Urbana. Taller courses take up all of the students time tho, and you can feel the stress in other classrooms when delivery is near. Geografia Urbana was really interesting, and also had a lot of group work which was a plus for the exams. Español para Extranjeros, I would only reccomend if you get credits for it, as I didn't get anything out of it.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The supermarkets are really expensive, so would reccomend going to the weekend markets. I have also used a lot of money to eat out and travel.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Supermarkets were more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I know there is a lot of social clubs and soccer teams, but I honestly didn't look much into it.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Different talks

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Didn't try any of them

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of good hiking opportuinities in Santiago and just outside. My favorit My favorite places are Pucón, Laguna del Maule, Pichilemu and Northern Chile.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I would say easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I would say that Chileans are maybe a bit more "reserved" than other South Americans, so sometimes you might be the one to start the conversation

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The work life balance in uni is difficult. The Chileans work A LOT and it's sometimes difficult when you have to coordinate group work. Also the Chilean spanish is hard

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The generousity of the people. It's also interesting to see how the culture chances from south to north

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) Make friends with the chileans in your class. The courses with field trips are a good way to do that. 2) Don't rely too much on the original course schedule/plan. Something a teacher says one day might not count the next. 3) Choose the fun courses and look up exam forms.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not necessarily for UCHILE. But for traveling a creditcard is essential (especially for car rental) as you can't use your debit card all the time.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends i made and the opportunity to travel as much as i have.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The winter was tough. There is no heating in most of the houses, so you never really get warm in those months. The hot water bottle saved me. Also that even after a whole semester here, the thick chilean dialect is stil impossible to understand.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
